result.builder:
Make one pull request that meets every acceptance line of issue https://github.com/o/strutil/issues/7 (padLeft for invoice numbers).

Context from the current repository: index.js is an ES module (package.json has "type": "module") that exports capitalize, slugify and truncate. README.md has sections `## capitalize(s)` and `## truncate(s, n)` but NO section for slugify. Tests live in test/strutil.test.js and run with `npm test` (`node --test`).

Steps:
1. In index.js add and export `padLeft(s, width, fill)` with a short doc comment like the other functions. It must pad `s` on the left with `fill` until the result is `width` characters long; when `fill` is not given (undefined) use a single space. When `s.length >= width`, return `s` unchanged. `String.prototype.padStart(width, fill ?? ' ')` meets this. Example: padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042'; padLeft('42', 5) === '   42'; padLeft('12345', 3, '0') === '12345'; padLeft('abc', 3, '0') === 'abc'. Do not change the behaviour of the existing functions.
2. In README.md add a section for every function index.js exports, in the same style as the existing ones (`## name(params)` heading followed by a one-line description). That means adding `## padLeft(s, width, fill)` (mention the space default and the unchanged-when-long case) AND adding the missing `## slugify(s)` section (lower case, words joined by dashes). Keep the existing capitalize, truncate and Tests sections.
3. In test/strutil.test.js import padLeft and add tests covering: zero padding ('42', 5, '0' -> '00042'), default space fill ('42', 5 -> '   42'), and unchanged return when s is already width or longer (equal length and longer).
4. Run `npm test` and make sure it passes with no failures. Before opening the pull request, also confirm every name exported from index.js has a `## <name>(` heading in README.md.
5. Open the pull request referencing issue #7.
result.verifier:
Check the pull request for issue https://github.com/o/strutil/issues/7 at its head commit. Run `npm install` only if package.json gained dependencies (it has none today). Run every command from the repository root. There is one check per expect line, in order.

Check 1 — expect: "index.js exports padLeft(s, width, fill), which pads s on the left with fill (a space when fill is not given) to width characters"
Run:
`node --input-type=module -e "import * as m from './index.js'; const r=[typeof m.padLeft, JSON.stringify(m.padLeft('42',5,'0')), JSON.stringify(m.padLeft('42',5)), JSON.stringify(m.padLeft('7',3,'x')), JSON.stringify(m.padLeft('',4,'0'))]; console.log(r.join(' '))"`
PASS: output is exactly `function "00042" "   42" "xx7" "0000"` (padLeft is an exported function; padding with the given fill on the left reaches width characters; with no fill the padding is spaces). FAIL: padLeft is not exported, the call throws, or any value differs (wrong side, wrong length, or a non-space default fill).

Check 2 — expect: "padLeft returns s unchanged when s is already width characters or longer"
Run:
`node --input-type=module -e "import {padLeft} from './index.js'; console.log(JSON.stringify([padLeft('12345',5,'0'), padLeft('123456',3,'0'), padLeft('abc',3), padLeft('abcd',2)]))"`
PASS: output is exactly `["12345","123456","abc","abcd"]`. FAIL: any string is padded, truncated or otherwise changed, or the call throws.

Check 3 — expect: "README.md has a section for every function index.js exports"
Run:
`node --input-type=module -e "import * as m from './index.js'; import fs from 'node:fs'; const md=fs.readFileSync('README.md','utf8'); const fns=Object.keys(m).filter(k=>typeof m[k]==='function'); const missing=fns.filter(f=>!new RegExp('^#+\\s+'+f+'\\b','m').test(md)); console.log('exports:',fns.join(','),'missing:',missing.join(',')||'none')"`
Then open README.md and confirm each such heading is followed by text describing that function.
PASS: `missing: none` is printed and each exported function (this must include capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft, plus any other exported function) has its own README heading with a description under it. FAIL: any exported function has no section — note that slugify had no README section before this change, so a PR that only adds padLeft fails this check.

Check 4 — expect: "npm test passes"
Run: `npm test`
PASS: exit code 0 and the summary shows `# fail 0`. FAIL: non-zero exit code or any failing test.

Advisory (not part of PASS/FAIL):
- Check that the existing functions capitalize, slugify and truncate behave as before (e.g. the original tests in test/strutil.test.js still exist and pass).
- It is good if the PR adds tests for padLeft covering default fill and the unchanged-when-long case.
